_meta.indication: Treatment of toxic plasma methotrexate concentrations (>1 micromole per liter) in patients with delayed methotrexate clearance due to impaired renal function

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 006 (PR001-CLN-rpt006), the NCI PD study, "Special Exception Protocol for the Use of Carboxypeptidase-G2 for MTX Toxicity"
pivotal_trials.phase: Open-label, nonrandomized compassionate-use (special exception) protocol; no formal phase designation
pivotal_trials.design: Historically-controlled, multicenter, single-arm clinical trial (methotrexate excretion curves used as the historical control)
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with toxic plasma methotrexate concentrations (>1 micromol/L) and severely delayed methotrexate clearance due to renal dysfunction
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of patients achieving a rapid (≤ 15 minutes) and sustained (≥ 8 days) clinically important reduction (RSCIR) in plasma methotrexate concentration, defined as attainment of plasma methotrexate ≤ 1 micromol/L at 15 minutes sustained for up to 8 days
pivotal_trials.n: FDA per-protocol efficacy population of 22 patients (applicant assessment based on 27 patients)
pivotal_trials.result: 10 of 22 patients achieved RSCIR [45% (95% CI 27, 65)]; all 22 patients had ≥ 97% reduction in plasma methotrexate within 15 minutes

key_safety: Among 290 patients in the safety evaluation, 21 (7%) had VORAXAZE-related adverse reactions, mostly Grade 1 or 2; most common (>1%) were paresthesias (2%), flushing (2%), nausea/vomiting (2%), headache (1%) and hypotension (1%). Serious allergic reactions, including anaphylaxis, occurred in less than 1% of patients.
target_moa: Glucarpidase is a bacterial carboxypeptidase enzyme that hydrolyzes methotrexate to two inactive metabolites (DAMPA and glutamate), rapidly reducing plasma methotrexate concentrations
modality: enzyme (recombinant carboxypeptidase enzyme produced by genetically-modified E. coli)

rems.type: A REMS is not required to ensure safe and effective use of Voraxaze

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to the Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee because the application did not raise significant public health issues

summary.text: Voraxaze received Fast Track designation (granted 1/5/2007) and was submitted as a rolling review, with the final portion completed on July 18, 2011. The BLA was granted Priority review and approved on a traditional (full) approval basis. Orphan drug exclusivity was granted for the indication. The application was not referred to an advisory committee.
